design_upstream: Augrant causal magic and skill progression

Ledger Shard.effect: pulls subtly toward genuine magical claims, keyed links, prepared transfers, or bound relationships
limitations: does not reveal whether the connection is hostile
does not identify who created it
does not reveal what lies at the other end automatically

known_techniques.name: Waymark
known_techniques.summary: Prepare a small anchor on a valid surface. Slow, visible, and physically vulnerable.

known_techniques.name: Vector Knot
known_techniques.summary: Redirect a small amount of existing momentum between a moving source and a compatible receiver. Strongest against committed motion.

known_techniques.name: Resonance Sense
known_techniques.summary: Slow observation can detect nearby prepared marks, active transfer effects, or strong residual magical disturbance; it is not omniscient.

limits: Poor geometry or an incompatible receiver can make a transfer fail.
Using magic under pressure requires concentration and can be interrupted.

canonical_facts: Dunmarrow's gate closes in roughly forty minutes.
Four bodies hang from the execution tree outside town.
One body moved.
Two gate guards have seen the player approaching but appear not to have noticed the movement.
Fresh muddy footprints lead from Dunmarrow to the tree and do not return.
A small geometric transfer symbol is cut into the bark beneath the fourth body.
The Black Tithe remains a working central mystery, not a predetermined single explanation.

The sensed effect appears to be actively redirecting motion through the ditch water rather than simply moving the water directly.
The tree carving and the ditch disturbance appear to participate in the same transfer geometry, but the exact relationship is not yet understood.
The player directly asked the concealed ditch entity whether it was their enemy.
The player shouted to alert the Dunmarrow gate guards while keeping the concealed ditch entity in view.
The concealed entity had previously said it was not the player's enemy unless made into one and demanded that the hanging man be cut down.
The player rushed to the execution tree and cut through the active transfer carving with the long knife.
A strong technical read let the player sever the geometry cleanly rather than merely damaging the bark.
The transfer structure collapsed immediately.
The abnormal motion in the ditch ceased.
The hanging man's movements stopped feeding the ditch effect.
The concealed entity lost part of whatever effect had hidden or sustained it.
The player chose to help the hanging man rather than pursue the fleeing entity.
The player cut the hanging man down without causing a serious fall.
The hanging man was alive but weak, with obvious neck compression and breathing difficulty.
The player immediately explained the active transfer mark, the hidden ditch figure, and the abnormal water movement to the approaching guard.
The concealed figure escaped farther along the drainage ditch while attention shifted to the victim.
The player chose not to pursue the escaped entity or investigate the missing boot.
The player left Edrin Vale and the execution-site evidence in the guards' custody.
Dunmarrow closes its town gates at dusk, but there is no established general stay-indoors curfew.
The player chose to meet Dunmarrow's reeve immediately after entering town.
The meeting takes place in the gatehouse while Edrin Vale is being treated nearby.

The player gave Reeve Maelin Voss a complete truthful account of the execution-ground incident, including speaking to the concealed entity, using Resonance Sense, the entity's demand to cut Edrin down, the transfer link, alerting the guards, severing the mark, seeing the fleeing figure, and Edrin's missing boot.

After the dormant bell tower rang and Resonance Sense reacted, the player asked Reeve Maelin Voss whether she wanted to investigate it.
The player urged the group to hurry to the old bell tower.
The player, Reeve Maelin Voss, and two watchmen reached the tower without stopping to investigate anything else en route.
The player ordered the group to stay together: investigate below the bell tower first, then go upstairs.
The player explicitly checked whether anyone in the group had a shield before committing.
The player attempted to sever the active transfer path beneath the bell tower using the same principle as at the execution tree.
The older network contained redundant/overflow routing. The cut did not stop the system; it caused a violent local discharge through the player's knife and arm.
The player took 4 damage, dropped the knife, and suffered temporary numbness/shock in the weapon hand.
The discharge fed additional motion into the bell above, causing it to ring again.
The failure revealed that this network reroutes interrupted transfer rather than simply collapsing when one path is cut.
After the failed cut, the player recovered the knife with the left hand and paused to observe the underground bell-tower transfer network before going upstairs.
A strong observation showed the basin objects act as person-specific anchors, while the iron rods carry transferred mechanical energy upward.
The network has redundant channels, but the rerouting is not instantaneous: there are brief moments where pressure shifts between paths.
The bell above is acting as a major receiver/reservoir and is currently closer to another discharge than before.
The player identified that blindly cutting more channels is likely to worsen the situation.
The player ordered a shield-and-reach formation on the spiral stair.
Harl holds the choke point with shield raised while Joren uses the spear from behind him; the player remains behind them due to the impaired right hand.
During the stairwell fight, the player used Vector Knot against the robed man's committed downhill lunge.
The player redirected a small portion of the attacker's existing momentum sideways and downward into the inner stair geometry rather than trying to stop him outright.

The player attacked the prone robed man with the long knife using the left hand while the right remained impaired.

The player ordered the group to hold formation and stop attacking the bell-linked man.

The connection has a narrow synchronization point just below the left side of the jaw where three carved lines converge.
The bell is receiving the man's movement and physiological shock as transferable mechanical input.

A brief disruption of rhythm, pressure, or alignment at the convergence point may be enough to desynchronize the coupling.

After demonstrating the full integrated sequence cleanly under unpredictable hostile timing, the player unlocked the combat technique Stored Reversal.

Stored Reversal is a constrained momentum-transfer technique: spend 1 Resonance when a readable physical strike or shove is incoming; capture only a safe fraction, retain it through whole-body structure for an instant, then release it through immediate movement or a compatible held weapon.

Stored Reversal cannot erase an attack, cannot safely catch arbitrary mass or unstable vectors, still allows ordinary impact to occur, and can injure the player on bad geometry, overload, or failed routing.
